title: TS SDK: bridge helpers and ergonomic examples for async-iterable ↔ Web Streams
creator: Marco Rivera
description:
Problem: TypeScript SDK users need idiomatic, low-friction helpers to move between AsyncIterable<T> and Web ReadableStream<T> (and vice-versa) across runtime environments (browser, Deno, Node). Current examples are fragmented: some teams use AsyncIterables, others use Web Streams; mismatch causes copy/paste errors, memory retention bugs, and inconsistent retry/cancellation semantics.

Goal: Provide a small, well-tested set of exported helpers plus a set of cookbook examples demonstrating: 1) conversion helpers AsyncIterable -> ReadableStream and ReadableStream -> AsyncIterable, 2) recommended retry patterns for streaming responses (resume, idempotency keys, backoff), 3) consumer ergonomics for common patterns (line-delimited tokens, JSON-framed messages, function-calling events), and 4) guidance for Node.js vs browser polyfills.

Non-goals: Implement a full streaming protocol (we surface primitives only); decide cross-runtime polyfill policy — we will document polyfills rather than bundle them.

Proposed API (exported from @redwood/sdk/streams):
- toReadableStream<T>(source: AsyncIterable<T>, options?: {cancelable?: boolean, highWaterMark?: number}): ReadableStream<T>
- toAsyncIterable<T>(stream: ReadableStream<T>, options?: {signal?: AbortSignal, chunkFormatter?: (chunk: any) => T}): AsyncIterable<T>
- streamWithRetries<T>(factory: () => Promise<ReadableStream<T> | AsyncIterable<T>>, opts?: {maxRetries?: number, backoffMs?: number, idempotencyKey?: string, onRetry?: (attempt:number)=>void}): AsyncIterable<T>
- streamFramer<T>(iterable: AsyncIterable<Uint8Array>, opts?: {delimiter?: Uint8Array | string, maxFrameBytes?: number}): AsyncIterable<Uint8Array | string>

Acceptance criteria:
- Helper functions implemented and exported with full TypeScript types and JSDoc.
- Unit tests covering conversions, large-stream memory behavior, cancellation, and basic retry logic.
- Integration examples in the SDK samples repo showing: (a) browser fetch + Response.body -> toAsyncIterable -> for-await loop, (b) WebSocket binary messages -> toReadableStream -> SDK consumer, (c) Node fetch-edge-case with AbortController, (d) example showing streamWithRetries resuming from fresh connection using idempotency token.
- Performance regression <= 5% for small messages and acceptable memory for large streaming responses (validated by a microbench).

Design trade-offs and rationale:
- Opt for minimal surface: users can compose primitives for advanced cases. The helpers should remain tiny (no heavy runtime deps).
- Retry strategy: streaming retries can only guarantee resume semantics for idempotent streams. We will add metadata guidance (server must support 'resume_offset' headers) but not attempt to encode a full protocol.
- Backpressure: Web Streams provide built-in backpressure for consumers in browser; AsyncIterable paths rely on consumer pacing. We provide optional highWaterMark and recommend consumers use for-await to naturally apply backpressure (documented examples).
- Polyfills: Document polyfill recommendations (web-streams-polyfill, node:stream/web) instead of bundling to avoid doubling package size and duplicated runtime behavior.

Open questions:
- Should streamWithRetries attempt automatic partial-resume when the service returns a 'resume-offset' header? (proposed: opt-in via opts.resumeStrategy = 'none' | 'server-offset' and only enabled if server advertises support)
- How aggressive should default maxRetries be for streaming vs single-response APIs? (proposal: defaults: maxRetries=2 for streaming, exponential backoff starting at 200ms)

Docs & examples to ship with PR:
- docs/streams.md (cookbook) w/ copy-paste examples for browser & node.
- samples/streams/browser-resume.html and samples/streams/node-resume.ts with small local server to simulate dropped connections.

Benchmarks and testing plan:
- Microbench: stream 10M small (32B) tokens and measure memory and throughput in Node 20 LTS and Chromium 118 using headless harness.
- Stress tests: concurrent consumer count (1, 10, 50) to validate throttling and GC behavior.
- CI: add e2e matrix job for Node and Chrome headless to run examples and smoke-test conversions.

Artifacts & links:
- Confluence design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SDK/pages/STREAM-Interop (internal)
- GitHub draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1542 (WIP)
- Prototype code sandbox: https://codesandbox.io/s/redwood-stream-bridge-proto (internal example)

Security considerations:
- Streaming helpers accept arbitrary user-provided formatters; we will document that untrusted binary framing must be validated by consumers. No secrets/state are captured except optional idempotencyKey metadata; ensure that the key is not logged.

Rollout plan:
- Merge helpers behind a feature flag (sdk.streamingInterop = true) for one release to surface early adoption and gather feedback. After 1 minor release of usage, flip on by default and promote cookbook in onboarding.
comments: 2026-02-12 — Marco: Created initial ticket and prototype for toReadableStream/toAsyncIterable conversions. Prototype passes simple smoke tests in Node and Chromium. Linked draft PR.

2026-02-18 — Lena: Review notes — prefer explicit AbortSignal param rather than implicit controller in helpers; added cancelable option and documented patterns for consumers to own AbortController. Asked for clear semantics when consumer throws inside for-await loops.

2026-02-25 — Marco: Updated API to include 'chunkFormatter' and 'highWaterMark' options. Added tests for consumer throw path — helpers now propagate errors and close underlying stream if cancelable=true.

2026-03-02 — Eng review meeting: Decided to make retry helper opt-in for server-offset resume. Default maxRetries=2. Action: add server-mock tests that simulate resume-offset header. Assigned to Lena to implement tests.

2026-03-06 — QA: Found memory retention when converting AsyncIterable<Uint8Array> -> ReadableStream when consumer abandons stream mid-way. Reproduction script added to samples. Fix planned: ensure we release held Buffers by use of tee() and immediate enqueue+release pattern.
2026-03-10 — Lena: Implemented fixes for buffer release and added test coverage. Draft PR updated (https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1542). Next: add cookbook examples and update docs.
